newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines cancels Camp John winner's bid.
newsitem.headline: Philippines cancels Camp John winner's bid.

text.p: The Philippine government's Bases Conversion Development Authority (Basecon) said on Wednesday it had declared a Philippine-Thai joint venture, Manuela Land & Houses (ML&H), "in default" for failing to meet a deadline to sign a lease agreement for the development of Camp John Hay.
Basecon chairman Victorino Basco said the project will instead be awarded to the second highest bidder, the Fil-Estate- Penta Capital Group, a Basecon statement said.
"ML&H automatically forfeited its 100 million peso deposit," the statement said.
"Rules are rules and they must be followed to the letter," the statement quoted Basco as saying.
"The government cannot do anything about it but to strictly enforce the rules to be fair with everbody. Otherwise, the integrity of the government bidding process will be compromised," it said.

Basecon, a government agency in charge of privatising former military bases, said it decided to cancel the winner's bid for the development of Camp John Hay after government lawyers said Basecon could not extend the deadline for ML&H to sign a 25-year lease agreement.
ML&H bid 1.58 billion pesos to develop and operate Camp John Hay, a former U.S. base in the northern Philippine hill resort of Baguio. Its bid was about four times bigger than the next offer.
The ML&H consortium comprises Thailand's Land and Houses Plc, AB Capital and Asia-Pacific and Planning Evaluation Co.
ML&H refused to sign the lease, saying that only 121.77 hectares of land was available for development and not the 247 hectares mentioned in the bid documents.
The deadline for ML&H to sign the lease agreement passed on September 8 and Basecon officials had met on Tuesday to consider whether the deadline should be extended.
The new winner of the deal is a group made up of Fil-Estate Land and local investment house Penta Capital Investment Corp.
